issues.quote: It had stopped. That is all I know of it. Aurèle loved that regulator more than most of his friends.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about the atelier regulator or any stopped clock. The stopped regulator is an added clock reading with no time attached.
issues.misreading: A solver could treat the stopped regulator as a time clue and try to tie its stoppage to the time of death or to the watch and bell readings, even though no reading of it is given.

issues.quote: In that house one notices clocks, Inspector. There are clocks in every room of it.
issues.fact: The fact sheet mentions only the salon clock (D3) and the watches and the temple bell. It does not say the house has a clock in every room.
issues.misreading: A solver could infer several clocks in the salon or nearby rooms and wonder whether the 'salon clock' is the only one meant, or whether another clock was the one that showed five minutes to ten.

issues.quote: Time devours all things, the clocks included.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no reason to think clocks bear on the time of death, and the physician's refusal to name a time is not in the sheet.
issues.misreading: The line reads as a pointed hint that the clocks are the key to the time of death, which the sheet does not support.
